dialog.body: Public Works, this is Kevin. Good morning.
Yeah, good morning. My name's Richard Wilcox. I'm calling about my recycling bin. It's gone. I put it out for pickup and after the truck came through, it just wasn't there.
Gone as in the truck took it, or somebody walked off with it, or the wind got it? Let me get a few details. Where are you located?
134 Malbone Road. That's up the North End, not far from the, uh, the main stretch. I rent the place, I'm not the owner, if that matters.
Okay, 134 Malbone Road. That's fine, renters call about this all the time. And what day was your pickup?

Well, it was this week. Um, with the storm, the snow-to-rain thing last weekend, Sunday into Monday, they pushed things back a day. So I put it out last night, and the truck came this morning, early. I left the bin at the curb.
Right, so you set it out Monday evening, and the truck came Tuesday. That's today. Okay, so this is just a couple hours ago.
Yeah. It was there at, I don't know, quarter to seven when I went to work out the window. Then I come back out a little after nine and there's nothing. No bin, no lid, nothing.
Did you check up and down the street? Sometimes the truck tips it and it rolls, or the wind with all that rain pushes it into a neighbor's yard or a snowbank.

I did. I walked down to the corner and back. Looked behind the hedges next door. There's a few of those big banks of plowed snow still sitting, I poked around some of those. [pause] Nothing. Neighbors' bins are all where they belong.
Okay. What color was it, and was it the city one, with the lid?
Blue, the city one. It's the regular size, the big rolling kind with the wheels. Had the lid on it. I never wrote my address on it or anything, so there's no marking.
Got it. Blue, city-issued, wheeled, no markings. I'm writing that down. So, one thing I should ask, is it possible the truck crew took it by mistake, or left it down the street?
Could be. I figured that was possible. Honestly I'd just like to know where it went. I don't want to go hunting all over the neighborhood.
Sure. I'll note that so the crew can look. Sometimes they find them at the end of the route, or one gets thrown in the back by accident.
Okay. Now, is there a fee for a replacement? I rent, so I'm not sure how that works. I didn't want to get a bill for something that I didn't lose, you know, on my end.

Good question. In general, if one's damaged or taken by the truck, they replace it. If it just disappears, it can depend on the situation. I don't want to tell you a flat yes or no on the charge. I'll put in the request and a supervisor can tell you whether there's a fee.
Fair enough. That's all I'm asking. I just want to know before I say yes to anything.
Understood. I'll write that you asked about the fee up front. Can I get a callback number?
Okay, 401-555-0195. And you said it's Richard Wilcox?
Yep. W-I-L-C-O-X.

Wilcox, got it. Hang on one second, I'm going to pull up the route for your street. [pause] Okay. I'm seeing the Malbone Road route did run this morning, a little behind because of the weather. That fits with what you saw.
Yeah, that fits. I heard the truck probably around seven, seven-fifteen.
The roads were wet but pretty clear by then. Not much snow left on the street. It's more the slush piles at the edges.
Yeah, that stuff hangs around. Have you got any kind of cart for the meantime? Because I can't promise a new one today.
I've got a plastic tub I can use. Nothing big. I'm not generating a lot, it's just me in there. It'll hold a week or so.
That works. Just keep the recycling clean and dry, and if you need to, set it out in the tub with a note and the crew will generally take it.
Okay, I can do that. So, should I do anything else on my end, like file something with the police, or is that overkill for a bin?
I wouldn't bother the police for a recycling bin, no. Just this report. If it turns up, great. If not, we handle the replacement.

Alright. Oh, one more thing, since I'm talking to you. I went down to the beach parking lot this morning, just to get some air before the day got going. It's pretty empty down there. A few walkers and nobody else. Not a car in half the lot.
Yeah, this time of year, it's quiet. Is there something you wanted to report about the lot, or just mentioning it?
No, no, just saying. Nothing wrong with it as far as I could see. Figured I'd mention it since I was out that way.
Okay, noted. Nothing to report there. Back to your bin, I'll flag this as a missing blue recycling bin, 134 Malbone Road, after Tuesday morning pickup, and mark the question about the fee.
That sounds right.
And I'll ask the crew supervisor to check whether it got picked up with the truck. Someone should call you back at that number, probably in a day or two.
A day or two is fine. I'm not in a rush. I've got the tub.
Great. Anything else I can help with today, Mr. Wilcox?
No, that's all of it. Thanks for your help, Kevin.
No problem. Have a good one, and good luck with the bin.
Thanks. Bye now.
